senses: The representation of a curve or surface in terms of a parametric equation.
Prone to, or suitable for, nibbling.
examples: Toss in wine and nibbly things to munch and it adds up to a unique shopping experience.

senses: Having only one color, represented by differing hues and tints. For example shades in a black and white television.
Perceptive of only one color; unable to distinguish colors; total color blindness.
Plain, dull, lifeless.
ety: From mono- + chromatic, mono- from Ancient Greek μόνος (mónos, “alone, only, sole, single”), chromatic from Ancient Greek χρῶμα (khrôma, “color”).

senses: The amount that a pocket would hold.
A small or moderate amount.
examples: White came to City Hall on Monday morning, entering through a basement window, with a gun and a pocketful of bullets.
This Government came in with a pocketful of promises. Every time the Prime Minister (Mr. Mulroney) saw two farmers at a crossroads he had five more promises to make.
Much more than a pocketful of fun awaits in this collection of rhymes and poems!

senses: Art that incorporates or mimics biological forms.
Virtual presence in another physical location by means of telecommunication technology.
examples: Telepresence robots that allow doctors or caretakers to interact with patients remotely are already in use in some hospitals and care facilities.

senses: The inability to speak, be it from psychological or physical cause.
ety: From French mutisme, from Latin mutus (“mute”), equivalent to mute + -ism.

senses: The treatment of seeds or bulbs by exposure to low temperatures so as to decrease the vegetative period or to cause the plant to flower or bear fruit more quickly.
examples: This low temperature requirement for flowering, called vernalization, begins at germination. Vernalization is assumed to occur at temperatures between 0 and 18°C (Ahrens and Loomis, 1963; Tirone and Metzer, 1970).
Species needing vernalization do not flower when grown in a warm climate.

senses: A letter of this syllabary.
ety: From Japanese 平(ひら)仮(が)名(な) (hiragana).

senses: Resembling or characteristic of a shark.
Indicating possible presence of sharks.
examples: They wanted to denounce the raids as a cruel misuse of crime-fighting resources — fishing for minnows instead of sharky predators.
He said the spot was very popular with surfers but was also known for being a "sharky area".

senses: Any member of the family Ostraciidae of often colorful, squared, bony fishes.
Having two wires, threads or filaments
Radiography of the urinary tract.
A little man.
examples: After one year she bore a beautiful Knabe; thereon the little manlet came to the bed and demanded him.

senses: Synonym of porringer (“a small cup or bowl”).
A Gothic pointed arch, or a rib of a Gothic vault.
ety: From late Middle English ogif, egeve, egeove, from Old French ogive, œgive, augive. Doublet of ogee.

senses: A fortified residence or encampment in Angola, or the military power associated with it.
A remote settlement in inland Brazil originally founded by fugitive slaves or their descendants.
ety: From Portuguese quilombo, and its source Kimbundu kilombo (“refuge, encampment”).
examples: The rugged, trackless and densely forested hills were almost impenetrable and the quilombos were spread widely.
Tiningu, whose pastel-coloured houses are home to 300 inhabitants, was originally a quilombo, a settlement founded by black fugitives from slavery.

senses: A material with binder and aggregate that is used to coat interior walls or to make interior mouldings.
A material with binder and aggregate that is used to coat exterior walls or to make exterior mouldings.
A work made of stucco; stuccowork.
ety: Borrowed from Italian stucco (“coating made of pulverised gypsum, plaster, stucco”) from Old Italian stucco, from Lombardic stucki, *stucchi (“crust, fragment, piece”) from Proto-Germanic *stukkiją (“stump, piece”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tewg- (“to shock, butt, impact”). Akin to German Stück (“piece”), Old Saxon stukki (“piece, fragment”) and Old English stycce. Related to stock.
examples: Many stuccos and paintings were also found on the mosaic floor of the presbyterium and choir; most of these are now in the Bardo Museum in Tunis.

senses: The branch of microbiology that deals with the study of viruses and viral diseases.
Any song with French words, but more specifically a classic, lyric-driven French song.
ety: From French chanson f (“song”), from Latin cantio f. Doublet of cantion and canzone.

senses: The office of an archdeacon, or the term of that office
The residence, or territorial jurisdiction of an archdeacon
A male steelworker.
A stronger version of an argument that one is about to critically analyze.
ety: From steel + -man. For the second definition, coined as the inverse of straw man.
examples: I want to make that strawman into a steelman, but I eliminated "the pursuit of happiness" from my to-do list so many years ago that I don't even know where I'd begin.

senses: A modern Turkish unit of surface area equal to a decare (1000 m²), equivalent to the modern Greek stremma.
Various other units in other areas of the former Ottoman Empire, usually equated to the decare but sometimes varying (as in Iraq, where it is 2500 m²).
ety: From Hebrew דּוּנָם (dúnam) or Arabic دُونُم (dūnum), from Turkish dönüm, from dönmek (“to turn”). A probable calque of Byzantine Greek στρέμμα (strémma, “stremma”, literally “that which is turned”).

senses: Somebody or something which franks.
To squelch; to eliminate.
ety: Alteration of squelch, perhaps influenced in form by quench.
examples: We are proud to have had a part in quelching the evil ideologies that brought so much suffering to mankind.

senses: Inclined to purr; purring.
examples: I gingerly patted Carbonel's back. His ears twitched, and I felt a rumble go through his fur. He was purring! “You have a very purry cat,” I said to Ellie.

senses: A form of extruded Indian incense, lacking a core bamboo stick.
ety: Borrowed from Hindi धूप (dhūp), from Sanskrit धूप (dhūpa), from धूप् (dhūp, “to fumigate, perfume”, root) + Proto-Indo-European *-os.

senses: The practice of applying entrepreneurial skills and approaches within an established company.
Being creative with ideas and procedures
A person who flogs using a birch rod.
Like a noob.
examples: He griefed, spammed, begged to be an administrator and did many other nooby things.

senses: Characteristic of a Whig; liberal.
Characterized by a belief in inevitable progress, and tending to evaluate the past by the standards of the present; see Whig history.
examples: Finally, whiggish narratives, strewn with heroes, only hinder understanding of how the world works.
Because this whiggish view depends on the expectation of progress, liberal politicians are more suspectible to it than their conservative brethren.
Of course, the reason we know all this—the reason the episode keeps turning up in Whiggish histories of technology—is that Plato wrote it down.

senses: Becoming reddish; tinged with red.
ety: Circa 1820, from Latin rufescens, present participle of rufescere (“to become reddish”), from rufus (“red”).
examples: Flesh unchanging or slowly rufescent.

senses: Synonym of pimento, a cultivar of Capsicum annuum.
ety: From Spanish pimiento (“bell pepper; later any pepper”), from Latin pigmentum (“coloring; colorful thing”), from pingō (“to paint”) and -mentum (suffix denoting instruments and results of actions). Doublet of pigment, piment, and pimento.

senses: metre (US: meter), poetic measure
sphere of influence
ety: From Ancient Greek μέτρον (métron). Doublet of meter, metre, and mether.

senses: A toasted sandwich.
toaster or toastie maker
examples: I much prefer cheese-and-onion toasties to those with bacon.

senses: An instance of verbalizing.
An expert in bioethics
Single-minded focus or concentration as part of practising yoga.
In Arabian countries and in Pakistan, India and Bangladesh, a lawyer or an administrator; one acting on behalf of another.
A Japanese girl fashion trend involving dyeing the hair and tanning the skin.
ety: Borrowed from Japanese slang ガングロ (ganguro), from 顔 (gan, “face”) 黒 (kuro, “black”), in reference to the style of makeup intended to imitate a dark tan.
